conviction_note: A mild positive. DMS raised its full-year forecast at the H1 print in each of the last two years (Oct 2024 ordinary +16.6%, Oct 2025 +13.7%) and then beat the raised FY26 plan by 11%. The FY27 plan is flat on last year (ordinary 1,590 vs 1,581) even though Q1 ordinary profit rose 26.6% and margin went from 3.5% to 4.6%, and Q2 only needs operating profit of 256m against 294m a year ago to meet the H1 plan. So a H1 beat is likely and an FY raise is plausible, but neither is pre-released and there is no consensus. The FY raise is the one item that would add something, and it is a decision rather than a number, so p_up is 60 on a 3.0 scale (+0.6). Findings sum to +0.9: the guidance finding carries most of it, the visible H1 beat is near 0 and a naphtha-cost risk the company left out of guidance offsets a little.
bar: Company H1 plan (unchanged since 2026-05-15 and held at Q1 on 2026-07-28): revenue 13,900m, operating profit 555m, ordinary 585m, net 410m. FY plan: revenue 30,700m, operating profit 1,530m, ordinary 1,590m, net 1,100m, dividend 232 yen. Sources: https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/9782_20260728_act_20260728_153011_1 and https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=9782. There is no IFIS consensus ('対コンセンサス -' on Monex/IFIS, '--' on kabuyoho https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/report?bcode=9782), so the company plan is the only sourced bar and the findings that depend on it stay capped small. The +10% print_vs_bar is my estimate for H1 operating profit (about 610-650m) against 555m.
positioning_check: JPX short register: 0.0%, no disclosed position at or above 0.5%, unchanged (baseline as of 2026-10-26, https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html). kabutan shows the margin ratio as '－倍' and labels the name 制度信用 buy-only, not a 貸借銘柄, so there are no margin shorts and nothing to squeeze (https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=9782, 2026-10-27). The 20-day run-up of -4.22% is almost entirely the 110-yen interim ex-dividend drop on 2026-09-29 (3,435 to 3,290; Yahoo chart dividend event 110.0). Adjusted for that, the stock is flat into the print. No options and no skew. Turnover is thin at about ¥95m a day.

findings.finding: DMS has raised its full-year forecast together with its H1 results in each of the last two years: on 2024-10-24, ordinary 1,000m to 1,160m (+16.6%) with the dividend raised from 75 to 86 yen; on 2025-10-27, ordinary 1,250m to 1,421m (+13.7%) after H1 ordinary of 561m beat its own H1 plan of 390m by 44%. It then beat the raised FY26 plan by 11.3% (1,581m). The FY27 plan of 1,590m is flat on that actual, although Q1 ordinary profit rose 26.6% and margin rose from 3.5% to 4.6%. A FY raise today is plausible, and the plan was set below the company's own run-rate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The baseline's estimated reaction for the 2025-10-27 H1 print with the FY raise is +3.48% (2025-10-28), and for the 2024-10-24 H1 print with the FY raise it is +3.22%. Both dates are cadence-estimated. On 2026-07-28, Q1 +27% with the plan held: +2.45% the next day (kabutan: 'ＤＭＳが反発…２ケタ営業増益').
findings.why_not_priced: No analyst consensus exists for the market to hold a revised number. Ex-dividend adjusted, the stock is flat since August and below its post-Q1 level, and nothing has been pre-released (no 業績予想の修正 on TDnet or kabutan since 2026-07-28). If a raise were priced, the stock would have run up into the print or a consensus would sit above the plan. Neither is true. This is a decision the company has not announced, and the base rate is two of two.
findings.independence: https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/9782_20251027_act_20251027_153006_2 (IFIS/Monex, the 2025-10-27 raise to 1,421m) and https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/9782_20260515_act_20260515_153046_2 (FY26 beat the raised plan by 11.3%; FY27 plan +0.6%). These are separate documents but rest on the same company record. Q1 strength comes from the same Q1 短信 used in finding 2.

findings.finding: H1 is on course to beat the company's H1 plan. Q1 operating profit was 299m against an H1 plan of 555m, so Q2 needs only 256m against 294m in Q2 a year ago. Q1 ordinary progress was 55.4% against a 5-year average of 53.0%. Revenue is the weak line: Q1 was -3.8% on DM campaign deferrals, and the H1 revenue plan of 13,900m needs Q2 at +4.2% YoY.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-10-27, H1 ordinary profit beat its own plan by 44% and came out together with an FY raise; the baseline estimates +3.48% next day. The H1 line has not been tested on its own.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Anyone can compute the progress rate from the Q1 短信, and kabutan printed it (55.4% vs 53.0% average). What is not visible is Q2's actual margin. Sized near zero for that reason.
findings.independence: https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=9782 (quarterly table: Q2 FY26 OP 294m, Q1 FY27 OP 299m). This is the same company data, so it is not independent of finding 1's Q1 input.

findings.finding: Management told the Q1 call that the impact of the Middle East situation on materials (naphtha for DM packaging film) and on customer behaviour is NOT built into the forecast. That leaves Q2 margin risk, and gives a ready reason to hold the FY plan rather than raise it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance on this name. Q1 margin rose despite the same headwind, which management attributed to price negotiations.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The naphtha headwind is public macro news, and the company said in public that it is excluded. What the market cannot see is whether Q2 margin absorbed it and whether management cites it to hold the plan. Kept small as a macro-to-company transmission.
findings.independence: https://prtimes.jp/main/html/rd/p/000001323.000043465.html (Teikoku Databank: packaging and materials price hikes driven by naphtha supply worries; food sector, a proxy, dated mid-2026).

findings.finding: The dividend runs on a DOE 8% policy through FY2027 (FY26 DOE 7.85%; the 232-yen FY27 forecast is about 115% of forecast EPS). A profit beat therefore moves the dividend only marginally: FY26 went from a 228-yen forecast to 234 actual. A dividend surprise is unlikely to be the swing item this time, unlike the Oct 2024 raise from 75 to 86.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2024-10-24: a dividend raise alongside the FY raise, estimated at +3.22% together. A separate 466m buyback in August 2025 has an announcement date and reaction I could not establish.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The 7.1% yield is the stock's anchor (kabutan) and the policy is public. A small upside tail remains if a buyback is announced with results, as total return was 158% in FY26.
findings.independence: https://kabuyoho.jp/reportDps?bcode=9782 (dividend history: 242 / 234 / 232 yen). This page's text was seen only in search snippets, not opened as a document.

outside_window.finding: The medium-term plan ends in FY2027 after its targets were met a year early. A new plan and any new shareholder-return policy (the DOE 8% runs only to FY27) is more likely at the May 2027 full-year print than today.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: no consensus. The company raised FY at H1 in 2024 and 2025, and the FY27 plan is flat on FY26 actual despite Q1 +27% operating profit, so an upward revision is plausible but not pre-released. Returns: DOE 8% policy, interim 110 yen already paid (ex 2026-09-29); a dividend surprise is unlikely, and a buyback is possible but unevidenced. New-year guide: not applicable (H1 print). Quarter vs own 進捗率: Q1 ordinary 55.4% of the H1 plan against a 53.0% 5-year average, so H1 is likely at or above plan, and that is visible.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the capital_return finding (finding 4) as its upside tail; its announcement date and timing were not established, so it is not a separate finding.

baseline_tension: Agrees mildly with the small positive priced lean (+0.21, all from the run-up term). The -4.2% run-up is an ex-dividend artefact rather than selling, so neither the run-up nor positioning (zero shorts, no margin shorts) argues for or against. The strongest negative the release could carry is a held FY plan citing naphtha costs together with an H1 revenue miss. I looked for it, it is filed as finding 3, and with no consensus to disappoint it would probably cost about 1-2%.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a series the market already has): the H1-beat finding rests on a 進捗率 anyone can compute from the Q1 短信, so it moved from +0.4 to +0.2. The rule is written for negatives; I applied its logic to this positive because the fact is equally visible.
Rule 2 (negatives outnumber positives): checked. This name is a net positive, and the one negative (naphtha) is a macro proxy kept small. p_up unchanged at 60.
Nothing else changed: the guidance finding (+1.0), the naphtha finding (-0.4), the DOE finding (+0.1), abs_move_pct 3.0 and p_up 60 all stand.
